headline: Approved a collective bargaining agreement with Hamden firefighters, a 2025-2026 budget transfer, and authority to apply for a federal justice grant.
summary: The council heard a presentation from the Hamden Food Collaborative and received public comment from four people. Members unanimously approved three items: a firefighters' contract, a budget transfer for the Purchasing Division, and authority to apply for and spend a federal justice grant.
decisions: Approved the collective bargaining agreement between the Town of Hamden and IAFF, Local 2687 Hamden Professional Firefighters, 10-0 unanimously.
Approved the intradepartmental transfer in the 2025-2026 fiscal year budget for the Finance Purchasing Division, unanimously.
Approved authority to apply for and, if awarded, accept and spend funds from the 2025 Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant, unanimously.

1. CALL OF THE MEETING AND TAKING OF THE ROLE 
Legislative Council Meeting, September 14, 2026 – 7:00pm.  The meeting was called to 
order by Pro Tem Cardwell at 7:10pm with the members noted above in attendance.  
Council member Teodosio joined while the meeting was in progress.  
  
 
Leadership Update – Pro Tem Cardwell called attention to recent changes to the 
Council agendas noting that Council President Kiely and Council Attorney Mednick 
have been working to return the process to compliance with the Council’s Standing 
Rules. 
2. REPORT OF DEPARTMENTS, BOARDS, COMMISSIONS, AND COUNCIL LIAISONS 
Updated Board and Commission Meetings - Pro Tem Cardwell pointed out that upcoming 
Board and Commission meeting information has been shared on the Committee agendas 
and encouraged the public to review it at their convenience. 
 
Department Head Updates – Pro Tem explained that the agenda notation indicating that 
we had not received updates from the department heads crossed with the receipt of the 
year-to-date updates, which he noted would be available for review, most likely for the 
next meeting.  
 
Council Liaison Updates – there were no updates for this evening’s meeting. 
  
  
3. PUBLIC INPUT SESSION AND CORRESPONDENCE 
For this evening, there were approximately 13 people joining via Zoom and about 20 in 
the Chamber.  
 
The public input session was opened at approximately 7:20pm.  Four members of the 
public came forward to provide public comment.  The Public Input session was closed at 
approximately 7:30pm.  Pro Tem Cardwell also announced that written public input was 
received and would be submitted for the record. 
  
4. CONSENT CALENDAR 
There were no items for the Consent Calendar for this evening’s meeting.  
5. REGULAR AGENDA DELIBERATION AND ACTION   
  1. Presentation by the Hamden Food Collaborative and Invitation to Upcoming 
Community Event
Representatives of the Hamden Food Collaborative provided an overview of 
the Collaborative's mission, current food security initiatives, and community 
partnerships. The presentation also highlighted ongoing programs, emerging 
needs, and opportunities for future collaboration.  
  2. Acceptance of Items Sent to Council for Submission Calendar 
 
Pro Tem Cardwell reviewed each of the Submission Calendar items received 
by the Council. He then called for a motion to accept the items.  The motion 
was made by Council member Foley, Seconded by Council member Osmanu. 
Vote: All in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions.  Motion to accept passed 
unanimously.  
6. RECESS FOR STANDING COMMITTEE MEETINGS  
Motion to recess for the committee meetings was made by Council member Figlar and 
seconded by Majority Leader Gallagher. 
Vote: All were in favor. 
 
Motion to come out of recess was made by Council member Osmanu and seconded by 
Council member Figlar. 
Vote: All were in favor.

Jeron Alston,
